title: Holy basil tincture for chronic stress
subtitle: A tulsi root tincture for cortisol-related fatigue and chronic stress
excerpt: Holy basil (tulsi) leaf macerated in 40% vodka for four to six weeks, then taken as a daily adaptogenic tincture for chronic stress and cortisol-related fatigue. Two to three ml in water twice daily for a three-month course. Not for use in pregnancy, and monitor blood sugar closely if on diabetes medication.
sourceNotes: WHO monograph on Ocimum tenuiflorum (2011) : pharmacology, traditional uses, adaptogenic action. Bhargava and Singh (1981), Journal of Pharmacy and Pharmacology : clinical study on stress-reducing properties. EMA HMPC assessment on Ocimum tenuiflorum : traditional-use framing in western herbal practice. Tincture preparation follows British Herbal Pharmacopoeia folk-tincture conventions (1 part dried leaf : 5 parts 40% spirit). Drug-interaction notes for anticoagulants and hypoglycaemic activity from WHO monograph and EMA assessment.

recipe.yieldDescription: About 120 ml tincture (approximately 40 doses at 3 ml each)
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Maceration takes 4 to 6 weeks. The finished tincture keeps 2 years in dark glass.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Store in amber glass in a cool dark cupboard. Keeps 2 years from the strain date.

glossaryTerms.definition: A term used in herbal medicine for herbs traditionally associated with supporting the body's capacity to cope with sustained stress. The term describes a functional category, not a biochemical mechanism.

projectSchedule.title: Start your tincture
projectSchedule.body: Pack the dried holy basil leaf into a clean maceration jar. Pour over the 40% vodka until the herb is fully submerged with at least 2 cm of liquid above. Seal tightly and label with the herb name, the spirit percentage, and today's date. Store in a cool dark cupboard.

projectSchedule.title: Check the liquid level
projectSchedule.body: Open the jar and check the vodka still fully covers the herb. Top up with a little more 40% vodka if needed. Give the jar a gentle shake and return it to the cupboard.

projectSchedule.title: Taste and check
projectSchedule.body: Taste a few drops from a small spoon. The tincture should have a clove-like, slightly spicy warmth with an herby base note. The liquid should be a warm green-brown. Return to the cupboard for another two weeks.

projectSchedule.title: Strain and bottle
projectSchedule.body: Your tincture is ready. Line a sieve with a double layer of muslin over a clean jug. Pour through and press the spent herb firmly. Funnel into amber dropper bottles. Label with the herb, spirit percentage, and strain date.

content.text: Holy basil
alcohol extract
is dried holy basil (tulsi) leaf macerated in 40% vodka for four to six weeks to produce a concentrated
alcohol extract
for chronic stress and cortisol-related fatigue. Holy basil is an
adaptogen
with deep roots in Ayurvedic practice and a growing place in western herbal medicine for sustained stress, low energy, and the kind of flatness that follows long periods of pressure. The
alcohol extract

path is more concentrated than a daily infusion; it suits a defined three-month course rather than an open-ended daily tea. The ratio is one part dried leaf to five parts 40% spirit by weight. The finished
alcohol extract
has a warm, clove-spice character. It keeps two years in dark glass.

attrs.title: Precautions
attrs.body: Not medical advice. Consult a qualified herbalist or doctor for ongoing or serious symptoms. Pregnancy: consult a herbalist or your midwife before using holy basil alcohol extract in pregnancy. the safety data at therapeutic alcohol extract doses in pregnancy is limited. Drug interactions: holy basil has mild antiplatelet activity. Readers on warfarin, aspirin, or other anticoagulants should consult their prescriber before using therapeutic doses. Blood sugar: holy basil can lower blood sugar. Readers on metformin, insulin, or any diabetes medication should monitor blood glucose more closely if they start this alcohol extract, and discuss it with their prescriber. Course length: take for three months, then review.

content.text: Ingredients

items.prepNote: dried holy basil (tulsi) leaf and aerial parts
plain 40% vodka; the alcohol percentage is important for preservation and extraction

content.text: Method
Step 1: Pack the jar

Pack the dried holy basil into a clean soaking period jar. Pour over the 40% vodka until the herb is fully covered with at least 2 cm of liquid above the top. Seal tightly. Label with the herb name, the spirit percentage, and today's date. Store in a cool, dark cupboard.
Step 2: Macerate four to six weeks
Shake the jar gently every few days. After two weeks, check the liquid level and top up with a little more vodka if the herb has absorbed it and any is exposed. At four weeks, taste a few drops: the
alcohol extract
should taste spicy-herby with the distinctive warm clove note of tulsi. Leave for up to six weeks for a stronger extraction.
Step 3: Strain and bottle

Line a sieve with a double layer of muslin over a clean jug. Pour the soaking period through and press the spent herb firmly to extract the last of the liquid. Funnel into clean amber dropper bottles. Label with the herb, spirit percentage, and strain date.
Dosing

Two to three ml (two to three droppers full) in a small glass of water, twice daily. Morning and early afternoon are the natural windows. Course length: three months. After three months, take a break of at least four weeks before considering another course. If energy and stress resilience do not improve after six to eight weeks, consult a herbalist.
Storage
Store in amber glass dropper bottles in a cool, dark cupboard. Keeps two years from the strain date.
When not to use this remedy

Consult your midwife or a herbalist before using in pregnancy. Do not combine with anticoagulant medication without medical supervision. If you are on diabetes medication, discuss this alcohol extract with your prescriber before starting and monitor blood sugar. See a doctor for persistent fatigue or stress that does not respond to lifestyle changes or herbal support after a reasonable course. these deserve medical assessment.
